1. <#
2. .SYNOPSIS
3. Configure a network adapter for FactoryTalk Logix Echo communication.
4. 
5. .DESCRIPTION
6. Rockwell QA64164 specifies that FactoryTalk Logix Echo controllers must use a Windows-configured
7. IPv4 address, not the loopback range (127.x.x.x). FactoryTalk Logix Echo can only bind a
8. controller to an IPv4 address Windows has already assigned to a NIC — it cannot invent a new
9. address on a subnet. This script:
10. 
11. 1. Detects the adapter Echo is already using (an address currently assigned to a controller must
12.    never be reused) and defaults to that adapter so a second controller lands on the same NIC.
13. 2. Otherwise lists available adapters and asks the user to select one, or create a new KM-TEST
14.    loopback adapter.
15. 3. Picks an IPv4 address ALREADY CONFIGURED on the selected adapter that no existing Echo
16.    controller is using — not a synthesized free address on the subnet. Only if every configured
17.    address is already claimed does it fall back to adding a brand-new address to the NIC.
18. 4. Never removes existing addresses from the adapter. A PLC/controller already bound to another
19.    address on this adapter keeps working.
20. 5. Sets the environment variable ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP for test execution.
21. 
22. If Echo cannot bind the newly assigned address (a "controller failed to set its IP address" or
23. "not yet synchronized" condition), restart the FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message Broker and Service
24. and retry - see docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md. This script does that automatically once before
25. giving up, and can be forced to do it up front with -RestartEchoServices.
26. 
27. .PARAMETER AdapterName
28. (Optional) The name of the adapter to configure. If not specified, the script auto-detects the
29. adapter Echo is already using, or prompts.
30. 
31. .PARAMETER IPAddress
32. (Optional) The static IPv4 address to assign. If not specified, the script picks an address
33. already configured on the chosen adapter that Echo is not currently using.
34. 
35. .PARAMETER RestartEchoServices
36. (Optional) Restart the FactoryTalk Logix Echo Windows services (Message Broker, then Service)
37. before configuring the adapter. Use this when a previous run reported that Echo could not bind
38. an assigned address.
39. 
40. .EXAMPLE
41. powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-echo-adapter.ps1
42. # Auto-detects the Echo adapter and picks an existing address on it that Echo isn't using.
43. 
44. .EXAMPLE
45. powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-echo-adapter.ps1 -AdapterName "KM-TEST" -IPAddress "192.168.127.5"
46. 
47. .EXAMPLE
48. powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-echo-adapter.ps1 -RestartEchoServices
49. 
50. .NOTES
51. Requires administrator privileges. Run from elevated PowerShell.
52. #>
53. 
54. param(
55.     [string]$AdapterName,
56.     [string]$IPAddress,
57.     [switch]$RestartEchoServices
58. )
59. 
60. $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
61. 
62. function Write-Status {
63.     param([string]$Message)
64.     Write-Host "`n[*] $Message" -ForegroundColor Cyan
65. }
66. 
67. function Write-Success {
68.     param([string]$Message)
69.     Write-Host "[OK] $Message" -ForegroundColor Green
70. }
71. 
72. function Write-Warning {
73.     param([string]$Message)
74.     Write-Host "[!] $Message" -ForegroundColor Yellow
75. }
76. 
77. function Write-ErrorMsg {
78.     param([string]$Message)
79.     Write-Host "[!!] $Message" -ForegroundColor Red
80. }
81. 
82. <#
83. .SYNOPSIS
84. Restart the FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message Broker and Service.
85. 
86. .DESCRIPTION
87. Rockwell support guidance for "controller failed to set its IP address" / addresses that never
88. synchronize is to restart the Message Broker (Echo's dependency) followed by the Echo Service
89. itself, then retry.
90. #>
91. function Restart-EchoServices {
92.     $broker = "FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message Broker"
93.     $service = "FactoryTalk Logix Echo Service"
94. 
95.     Write-Status "Restarting FactoryTalk Logix Echo services..."
96.     foreach ($svcName in @($service, $broker)) {
97.         $svc = Get-Service -Name $svcName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
98.         if (-not $svc) {
99.             Write-Warning "Service '$svcName' not found on this host; skipping."
100.             continue
101.         }
102.         if ($svc.Status -eq "Running") {
103.             Write-Host "  Stopping '$svcName'..."
104.             Stop-Service -Name $svcName -Force -ErrorAction Stop
105.             $svc.WaitForStatus("Stopped", (New-TimeSpan -Seconds 60))
106.         }
107.     }
108. 
109.     # Bring them back up in dependency order: Message Broker first, then the Echo Service.
110.     foreach ($svcName in @($broker, $service)) {
111.         $svc = Get-Service -Name $svcName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
112.         if (-not $svc) {
113.             continue
114.         }
115.         Write-Host "  Starting '$svcName'..."
116.         Start-Service -Name $svcName -ErrorAction Stop
117.         $svc.WaitForStatus("Running", (New-TimeSpan -Seconds 60))
118.         Write-Success "'$svcName' is running"
119.     }
120. 
121.     # Give the Echo Service a moment to finish initializing its API before the next call.
122.     Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
123. }
124. 
125. # Check for admin
126. if (-not ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal] [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)) {
127.     Write-ErrorMsg "This script requires administrator privileges. Run from elevated PowerShell."
128.     exit 1
129. }
130. 
131. Write-Status "FactoryTalk Logix Echo Network Adapter Configuration"
132. Write-Host "Rockwell QA64164 requires a non-loopback IPv4 address for Echo communication."
133. 
134. if ($RestartEchoServices) {
135.     Restart-EchoServices
136. }
137. 
138. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
139. # Guardrail: never reuse an IP address a controller already holds.
140. #
141. # Echo assigns controller addresses out of whichever adapter subnet is
142. # selected. If an operator has already configured a chassis/controller on an
143. # IP, colliding with it produces a hard-to-diagnose "address in use" or
144. # "not yet synchronized" failure much later in a test run. Detect existing
145. # Echo-assigned addresses up front and steer away from them.
146. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
147. function Get-EchoAssignedAddresses {
148.     <#
149.     .SYNOPSIS
150.     Returns every IPv4 address FactoryTalk Logix Echo currently reports as assigned to a
151.     controller, via the test harness's "echo-list-addresses" command, or $null if it cannot be
152.     determined (harness not built, or Echo unreachable).
153.     #>
154.     $harnessExe = Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..\tests\harness") `
155.         -Recurse -Filter "LogixEchoHarness.exe" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
156.         Select-Object -First 1
157.     if (-not $harnessExe) {
158.         return $null
159.     }
160. 
161.     try {
162.         $raw = & $harnessExe.FullName "echo-list-addresses" 2>$null
163.         if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
164.             return $null
165.         }
166.         if (-not $raw) {
167.             return @()
168.         }
169.         return @($raw | Where-Object { [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($_.Trim(), [ref]$null) })
170.     }
171.     catch {
172.         return $null
173.     }
174. }
175. 
176. function Select-UnusedAdapterAddress {
177.     <#
178.     .SYNOPSIS
179.     Return the first IPv4 address already configured on the adapter that Echo is not currently
180.     using for a controller.
181. 
182.     .DESCRIPTION
183.     FactoryTalk Logix Echo can only bind a controller to an IPv4 address that Windows has already
184.     assigned to a NIC (see IServiceApiClientV2.ListAvailableEthernetAddresses(), which enumerates
185.     configured addresses - it does not invent new ones on a subnet). The guardrail is therefore
186.     to pick among the adapter's EXISTING addresses, skipping whichever one(s) an existing Echo
187.     controller already holds, rather than synthesizing an arbitrary free host address that was
188.     never added to the NIC.
189.     #>
190.     param(
191.         [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$AdapterAddresses,
192.         [string[]]$InUse = @()
193.     )
194. 
195.     foreach ($candidate in $AdapterAddresses) {
196.         if ($candidate.StartsWith("127.") -or $candidate.StartsWith("169.254.")) {
197.             continue
198.         }
199.         if ($InUse -notcontains $candidate) {
200.             return $candidate
201.         }
202.     }
203. 
204.     return $null
205. }
206. 
207. # Get available adapters
208. $adapters = @(Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq "Up" -or $_.Status -eq "Disconnected" })
209. 
210. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
211. # Auto-detect the adapter Echo is already using, so a second/third controller
212. # lands on the same NIC instead of a caller picking an unrelated adapter.
213. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
214. $autoDetectedAdapter = $null
215. if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName)) {
216.     Write-Status "Checking for an adapter Echo is already configured on..."
217.     $priorEchoIp = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", "User")
218.     foreach ($candidate in $adapters) {
219.         $existing = Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $candidate.Name -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
220.             Where-Object { -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("127.") -and -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("169.254.") }
221.         if ($existing -and $priorEchoIp -and ($existing.IPAddress -contains $priorEchoIp)) {
222.             $autoDetectedAdapter = $candidate.Name
223.             Write-Success "Found existing Echo adapter '$($candidate.Name)' (holds previously configured $priorEchoIp)"
224.             break
225.         }
226.     }
227.     if (-not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
228.         Write-Host "No previously configured Echo adapter found; you will be prompted to choose one."
229.     }
230. }
231. 
232. # If no adapter name provided, ask user
233. if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName) -and -not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
234.     Write-Host ""
235.     Write-Host "Available network adapters:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
236.     $adapters | ForEach-Object -Begin { $i = 1 } -Process {
237.         Write-Host "  [$i] $($_.Name) - $($_.InterfaceDescription) (Status: $($_.Status))"
238.         $i++
239.     }
240.     Write-Host "  [N] Create new KM-TEST loopback adapter"
241.     Write-Host ""
242. 
243.     do {
244.         $choice = Read-Host "Select adapter [1-$($adapters.Count)|N]"
245. 
246.         if ($choice -eq "N" -or $choice -eq "n") {
247.             $adapterName = "KM-TEST"
248.             $createNew = $true
249.             break
250.         }
251. 
252.         if ([int]::TryParse($choice, [ref]$idx)) {
253.             if ($idx -ge 1 -and $idx -le $adapters.Count) {
254.                 $selectedAdapter = $adapters[$idx - 1]
255.                 $adapterName = $selectedAdapter.Name
256.                 $createNew = $false
257.                 break
258.             }
259.         }
260. 
261.         Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid selection. Please try again."
262.     } while ($true)
263. } elseif ($autoDetectedAdapter) {
264.     $adapterName = $autoDetectedAdapter
265.     $createNew = $false
266. } else {
267.     # Check if adapter exists
268.     $selected = $adapters | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $AdapterName }
269.     if ($selected) {
270.         $createNew = $false
271.         Write-Success "Using adapter: $AdapterName"
272.     } elseif ($AdapterName -eq "KM-TEST") {
273.         $createNew = $true
274.         Write-Success "Will create/use KM-TEST adapter"
275.     } else {
276.         Write-ErrorMsg "Adapter '$AdapterName' not found and is not 'KM-TEST'"
277.         exit 1
278.     }
279. }
280. 
281. # If creating new KM-TEST, do so now
282. if ($createNew) {
283.     $kmtest = Get-NetAdapter -Name "KM-TEST" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
284.     if ($kmtest) {
285.         Write-Success "KM-TEST adapter already exists"
286.     } else {
287.         Write-Status "Creating Microsoft Loopback Adapter (KM-TEST)..."
288.         try {
289.             $loopback = New-NetLoopbackAdapter -Name "KM-TEST" -ErrorAction Stop
290.             Write-Success "Created loopback adapter: $($loopback.Name)"
291.         }
292.         catch {
293.             Write-ErrorMsg "Failed to create loopback adapter: $_"
294.             Write-Host "`nAlternative: Create the adapter manually via Device Manager:"
295.             Write-Host "  1. Right-click Start Menu > Device Manager"
296.             Write-Host "  2. Action > Add legacy hardware"
297.             Write-Host "  3. Select 'Install the hardware that I manually select from a list'"
298.             Write-Host "  4. Choose 'Network Adapters'"
299.             Write-Host "  5. Select 'Microsoft' manufacturer, 'Microsoft Loopback Adapter'"
300.             Write-Host "  6. Name it 'KM-TEST'"
301.             Write-Host "  7. Return to this script after creation"
302.             exit 1
303.         }
304.     }
305. }
306. 
307. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
308. # Determine which addresses on the target adapter are already in use by Echo,
309. # so the guardrail can pick another address ALREADY CONFIGURED on the NIC that
310. # Echo is not using - not a synthesized free host address on the subnet. Echo
311. # can only bind a controller to an address Windows has already assigned to a
312. # NIC; it does not create new subnet addresses on its own.
313. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
314. $existingAdapterIPs = @(
315.     Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $adapterName -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
316.         Select-Object -ExpandProperty IPAddress
317. )
318. $echoAssigned = Get-EchoAssignedAddresses
319. if ($null -eq $echoAssigned) {
320.     Write-Warning "Could not query Echo's currently assigned addresses (harness not built, or Echo unreachable)."
321.     Write-Warning "Falling back to only the adapter's configured addresses for collision avoidance."
322.     $echoAssigned = @()
323. }
324. 
325. if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {
326.     Write-Status "Adapter '$adapterName' already has address(es) assigned:"
327.     $existingAdapterIPs | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $_" }
328.     Write-Warning "These will NOT be removed. A PLC/controller already configured on one of these must keep working."
329. }
330. 
331. # Prompt for IP address if not provided
332. if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($IPAddress)) {
333.     $suggested = Select-UnusedAdapterAddress -AdapterAddresses $existingAdapterIPs -InUse $echoAssigned
334. 
335.     if ($suggested) {
336.         Write-Host ""
337.         Write-Host "Address already configured on '$adapterName' that Echo is not using: $suggested" -ForegroundColor Cyan
338.         Write-Host "Press Enter to accept, or type a different non-loopback IPv4 address already on this NIC."
339.     } else {
340.         Write-Warning "Every address currently configured on '$adapterName' is already in use by an Echo controller."
341.         Write-Host "A new address must be added to the NIC before Echo can use it."
342.         Write-Host "Enter a non-loopback IPv4 address on the same subnet as this adapter (e.g. matching"
343.         Write-Host "the /24 of $($existingAdapterIPs -join ', '))."
344.     }
345.     Write-Host "CRITICAL: Do NOT use loopback addresses (127.x.x.x) - they cannot be used with Logix Designer"
346.     Write-Host ""
347. 
348.     do {
349.         if ($suggested) {
350.             $entered = Read-Host "IP Address [$suggested]"
351.             if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($entered)) {
352.                 $IPAddress = $suggested
353.             } else {
354.                 $IPAddress = $entered
355.             }
356.         } else {
357.             $IPAddress = Read-Host "IP Address"
358.         }
359. 
360.         # Validate IP format
361.         if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
362.             Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format. Please try again."
363.             continue
364.         }
365. 
366.         # Reject loopback addresses (127.x.x.x)
367.         if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
368.             Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
369.             Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
370.             Write-Host ""
371.             continue
372.         }
373. 
374.         # Reject any address already claimed by an existing Echo controller.
375.         if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
376.             Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
377.             Write-Host "Choose a different address to avoid colliding with a PLC that is already configured."
378.             Write-Host ""
379.             continue
380.         }
381. 
382.         Write-Success "IP address: $IPAddress"
383.         break
384.     } while ($true)
385. } else {
386.     # Validate provided IP
387.     if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
388.         Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format: $IPAddress"
389.         exit 1
390.     }
391. 
392.     if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
393.         Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
394.         Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
395.         exit 1
396.     }
397. 
398.     if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
399.         Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
400.         Write-Host "Pick a different address; reusing an address in use by another PLC will break it."
401.         exit 1
402.     }
403. 
404.     Write-Success "Using IP address: $IPAddress"
405. }
406. 
407. # Whether we still need to add $IPAddress to the adapter, or it is already
408. # configured there (the common case: Echo just wasn't using it yet).
409. $addressAlreadyOnAdapter = $existingAdapterIPs -contains $IPAddress
410. 
411. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
412. # Configure the adapter. If the address is already configured on the NIC
413. # (the common case - it's simply an address Echo isn't using yet), there is
414. # nothing to add. Existing addresses are never removed - a PLC/controller
415. # Echo already has configured on this adapter must keep working.
416. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
417. function Add-EchoAdapterAddress {
418.     param(
419.         [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$AdapterName,
420.         [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$IPAddress
421.     )
422. 
423.     New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $AdapterName -IPAddress $IPAddress -PrefixLength 24 -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
424.     Enable-NetAdapter -Name $AdapterName -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
425.     Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500
426. }
427. 
428. if ($addressAlreadyOnAdapter) {
429.     Write-Status "IP $IPAddress is already configured on adapter '$adapterName'; nothing to add."
430.     Enable-NetAdapter -Name $adapterName -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
431.     Write-Success "Adapter '$adapterName' enabled"
432. } else {
433.     Write-Status "Adding IP $IPAddress/24 to adapter '$adapterName' (existing addresses left untouched)..."
434.     try {
435.         Add-EchoAdapterAddress -AdapterName $adapterName -IPAddress $IPAddress
436.         Write-Success "Configured IP address: $IPAddress/24"
437.         Write-Success "Adapter '$adapterName' enabled"
438.     }
439.     catch {
440.         # Rockwell guidance: if Echo cannot pick up a newly assigned address, restart
441.         # the Message Broker and Echo Service, then retry once.
442.         Write-Warning "Failed to configure adapter on first attempt: $_"
443.         Write-Warning "Retrying after restarting FactoryTalk Logix Echo services..."
444.         try {
445.             Restart-EchoServices
446.             Add-EchoAdapterAddress -AdapterName $adapterName -IPAddress $IPAddress
447.             Write-Success "Configured IP address: $IPAddress/24 (after Echo service restart)"
448.         }
449.         catch {
450.             Write-ErrorMsg "Failed to configure adapter even after restarting Echo services: $_"
451.             exit 1
452.         }
453.     }
454. }
455. 
456. # Set the environment variable for the test harness
457. Write-Status "Setting environment variable ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP..."
458. try {
459.     [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", $IPAddress, "User")
460.     Write-Success "Environment variable set: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
461. }
462. catch {
463.     Write-ErrorMsg "Failed to set environment variable: $_"
464.     exit 1
465. }
466. 
467. # Summary
468. Write-Status "Echo adapter configuration complete"
469. Write-Success "Ready for test execution"
470. Write-Host ""
471. Write-Host "Configuration Summary:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
472. Write-Host "  Adapter:     $adapterName"
473. Write-Host "  IP Address:  $IPAddress/24"
474. Write-Host "  Echo IP Var: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
475. if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {
476.     Write-Host "  Preserved:   $($existingAdapterIPs -join ', ')"
477. }
478. Write-Host ""
479. Write-Host "To verify in PowerShell:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
480. Write-Host "  Get-NetAdapter -Name '$adapterName'"
481. Write-Host "  Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias '$adapterName' -AddressFamily IPv4"
482. Write-Host "  [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP', 'User')"
483. Write-Host ""
484. Write-Host "If Echo reports the controller could not set its IP address, rerun with:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
485. Write-Host "  -RestartEchoServices"
486. Write-Host ""
487. Write-Host "Note: Restart PowerShell to use the new environment variable in this session" -ForegroundColor Yellow
488. 
489. exit 0
490.

arguments.file_text:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Identify a network address for FactoryTalk Logix Echo communication and set ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP.

.DESCRIPTION
Rockwell QA64164 specifies that FactoryTalk Logix Echo controllers must use a Windows-configured
IPv4 address, not the loopback range (127.x.x.x). FactoryTalk Logix Echo can only bind a
controller to an IPv4 address Windows has already assigned to a NIC — it cannot invent a new
address on a subnet.

This script is READ-ONLY with respect to the network: it never adds, removes, or otherwise
modifies adapters or IP addresses, and never restarts services. It only inspects existing state
and helps you choose a value for ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP. Any NIC configuration (adding an address to
an adapter) or Windows service restart must be performed manually by an operator with
administrator privileges, per docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md.

This script:

1. Detects the adapter Echo is already using (an address currently assigned to a controller must
   never be reused) by matching a previously configured ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP, or lets you pick from
   the adapters currently present on this machine.
2. Queries Echo (via the harness's `echo-list-addresses` command) for every address a controller
   already holds.
3. Lists the IPv4 addresses already configured on the selected adapter and suggests one that no
   existing Echo controller is using — never proposing or accepting an address already claimed
   by a controller, and never a synthesized address that isn't actually configured on the NIC.
4. If every address already configured on the adapter is claimed by a controller, tells you a new
   address must be added to the NIC manually (this script will not do it) before Echo can use it.
5. Sets the environment variable ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP for test execution.

If Echo cannot bind an address (a "controller failed to set its IP address" or "not yet
synchronized" condition), the fix is to manually restart the FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message
Broker and Service (in that order: stop Service, stop Broker, start Broker, start Service) and
retry - see docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md. This script does not perform that restart.

.PARAMETER AdapterName
(Optional) The name of the adapter to inspect. If not specified, the script auto-detects the
adapter Echo is already using, or prompts you to choose from adapters present on this machine.

.PARAMETER IPAddress
(Optional) The static IPv4 address to use. If not specified, the script suggests an address
already configured on the chosen adapter that Echo is not currently using.

.EXAMPLE
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-echo-adapter.ps1
# Auto-detects the Echo adapter and suggests an existing address on it that Echo isn't using.

.EXAMPLE
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-echo-adapter.ps1 -AdapterName "Ethernet" -IPAddress "192.168.127.6"

.NOTES
Does not require administrator privileges. Performs no NIC or service changes.
#>

param(
    [string]$AdapterName,
    [string]$IPAddress
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Write-Status {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "`n[*] $Message" -ForegroundColor Cyan
}

function Write-Success {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[OK] $Message" -ForegroundColor Green
}

function Write-Warning {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[!] $Message" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

function Write-ErrorMsg {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[!!] $Message" -ForegroundColor Red
}

Write-Status "FactoryTalk Logix Echo Network Address Discovery"
Write-Host "Rockwell QA64164 requires a non-loopback IPv4 address for Echo communication."
Write-Host "This script does not modify any adapter or service; it only helps choose an address."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Guardrail: never reuse an IP address a controller already holds.
#
# Echo assigns controller addresses out of whichever adapter subnet is
# selected. If an operator has already configured a chassis/controller on an
# IP, colliding with it produces a hard-to-diagnose "address in use" or
# "not yet synchronized" failure much later in a test run. Detect existing
# Echo-assigned addresses up front and steer away from them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function Get-EchoAssignedAddresses {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns every IPv4 address FactoryTalk Logix Echo currently reports as assigned to a
    controller, via the test harness's "echo-list-addresses" command, or $null if it cannot be
    determined (harness not built, or Echo unreachable).
    #>
    $harnessExe = Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..\tests\harness") `
        -Recurse -Filter "LogixEchoHarness.exe" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $harnessExe) {
        return $null
    }

    try {
        $raw = & $harnessExe.FullName "echo-list-addresses" 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            return $null
        }
        if (-not $raw) {
            return @()
        }
        return @($raw | Where-Object { [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($_.Trim(), [ref]$null) })
    }
    catch {
        return $null
    }
}

function Select-UnusedAdapterAddress {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Return the first IPv4 address already configured on the adapter that Echo is not currently
    using for a controller.

    .DESCRIPTION
    FactoryTalk Logix Echo can only bind a controller to an IPv4 address that Windows has already
    assigned to a NIC (see IServiceApiClientV2.ListAvailableEthernetAddresses(), which enumerates
    configured addresses - it does not invent new ones on a subnet). The guardrail is therefore
    to pick among the adapter's EXISTING addresses, skipping whichever one(s) an existing Echo
    controller already holds, rather than synthesizing an arbitrary free host address that was
    never added to the NIC.
    #>
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$AdapterAddresses,
        [string[]]$InUse = @()
    )

    foreach ($candidate in $AdapterAddresses) {
        if ($candidate.StartsWith("127.") -or $candidate.StartsWith("169.254.")) {
            continue
        }
        if ($InUse -notcontains $candidate) {
            return $candidate
        }
    }

    return $null
}

# Get available adapters (read-only enumeration; nothing is created or changed)
$adapters = @(Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq "Up" -or $_.Status -eq "Disconnected" })

if ($adapters.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-ErrorMsg "No network adapters found on this machine."
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auto-detect the adapter Echo is already using, so a second/third controller
# lands on the same NIC instead of a caller picking an unrelated adapter.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$autoDetectedAdapter = $null
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName)) {
    Write-Status "Checking for an adapter Echo is already configured on..."
    $priorEchoIp = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", "User")
    foreach ($candidate in $adapters) {
        $existing = Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $candidate.Name -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("127.") -and -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("169.254.") }
        if ($existing -and $priorEchoIp -and ($existing.IPAddress -contains $priorEchoIp)) {
            $autoDetectedAdapter = $candidate.Name
            Write-Success "Found existing Echo adapter '$($candidate.Name)' (holds previously configured $priorEchoIp)"
            break
        }
    }
    if (-not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
        Write-Host "No previously configured Echo adapter found; you will be prompted to choose one."
    }
}

# If no adapter name provided, ask user to pick from adapters that already exist
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName) -and -not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Available network adapters:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $adapters | ForEach-Object -Begin { $i = 1 } -Process {
        Write-Host "  [$i] $($_.Name) - $($_.InterfaceDescription) (Status: $($_.Status))"
        $i++
    }
    Write-Host ""

    do {
        $choice = Read-Host "Select adapter [1-$($adapters.Count)]"

        if ([int]::TryParse($choice, [ref]$idx)) {
            if ($idx -ge 1 -and $idx -le $adapters.Count) {
                $selectedAdapter = $adapters[$idx - 1]
                $adapterName = $selectedAdapter.Name
                break
            }
        }

        Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid selection. Please try again."
    } while ($true)
} elseif ($autoDetectedAdapter) {
    $adapterName = $autoDetectedAdapter
} else {
    # Check if the requested adapter exists; this script never creates adapters
    $selected = $adapters | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $AdapterName }
    if ($selected) {
        Write-Success "Using adapter: $AdapterName"
    } else {
        Write-ErrorMsg "Adapter '$AdapterName' not found on this machine."
        Write-Host "This script does not create adapters. Available adapters:"
        $adapters | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $($_.Name) - $($_.InterfaceDescription)" }
        exit 1
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Determine which addresses on the target adapter are already in use by Echo,
# so the guardrail can suggest another address ALREADY CONFIGURED on the NIC
# that Echo is not using - not a synthesized free host address on the subnet.
# Echo can only bind a controller to an address Windows has already assigned
# to a NIC; it does not create new subnet addresses on its own, and neither
# does this script.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$existingAdapterIPs = @(
    Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $adapterName -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Select-Object -ExpandProperty IPAddress
)
$echoAssigned = Get-EchoAssignedAddresses
if ($null -eq $echoAssigned) {
    Write-Warning "Could not query Echo's currently assigned addresses (harness not built, or Echo unreachable)."
    Write-Warning "Falling back to only the adapter's configured addresses for collision avoidance."
    $echoAssigned = @()
}

if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Status "Adapter '$adapterName' has address(es) already configured:"
    $existingAdapterIPs | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $_" }
} else {
    Write-Warning "Adapter '$adapterName' has no IPv4 addresses configured."
    Write-Host "An administrator must add a non-loopback address to this adapter manually before"
    Write-Host "Echo can use it. This script will not do so."
}

# Choose an IP address if not provided
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($IPAddress)) {
    $suggested = Select-UnusedAdapterAddress -AdapterAddresses $existingAdapterIPs -InUse $echoAssigned

    if ($suggested) {
        Write-Host ""
        Write-Host "Address already configured on '$adapterName' that Echo is not using: $suggested" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        Write-Host "Press Enter to accept, or type a different non-loopback IPv4 address already on this NIC."
    } else {
        Write-Warning "Every address currently configured on '$adapterName' is already in use by an Echo controller."
        Write-Host "An administrator must manually add a new address to this NIC before Echo can use it"
        Write-Host "(this script will not modify the adapter). Once added, enter it below, or enter any"
        Write-Host "non-loopback IPv4 address already present on this adapter."
    }
    Write-Host "CRITICAL: Do NOT use loopback addresses (127.x.x.x) - they cannot be used with Logix Designer"
    Write-Host ""

    do {
        if ($suggested) {
            $entered = Read-Host "IP Address [$suggested]"
            if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($entered)) {
                $IPAddress = $suggested
            } else {
                $IPAddress = $entered
            }
        } else {
            $IPAddress = Read-Host "IP Address"
        }

        # Validate IP format
        if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
            Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format. Please try again."
            continue
        }

        # Reject loopback addresses (127.x.x.x)
        if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
            Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
            Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
            Write-Host ""
            continue
        }

        # Reject any address already claimed by an existing Echo controller.
        if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
            Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
            Write-Host "Choose a different address to avoid colliding with a PLC that is already configured."
            Write-Host ""
            continue
        }

        # Warn (but don't block) if the address isn't actually on the adapter yet - Echo
        # cannot use it until an administrator adds it manually.
        if ($existingAdapterIPs -notcontains $IPAddress) {
            Write-Warning "'$IPAddress' is not currently configured on adapter '$adapterName'."
            Write-Warning "An administrator must add it to the NIC manually before Echo can use it."
        }

        Write-Success "IP address: $IPAddress"
        break
    } while ($true)
} else {
    # Validate provided IP
    if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
        Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format: $IPAddress"
        exit 1
    }

    if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
        Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
        Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
        exit 1
    }

    if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
        Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
        Write-Host "Pick a different address; reusing an address in use by another PLC will break it."
        exit 1
    }

    if ($existingAdapterIPs -notcontains $IPAddress) {
        Write-Warning "'$IPAddress' is not currently configured on adapter '$adapterName'."
        Write-Warning "An administrator must add it to the NIC manually before Echo can use it."
    }

    Write-Success "Using IP address: $IPAddress"
}

# Set the environment variable for the test harness. This is the only change this script makes;
# it does not touch adapters, addresses, or services.
Write-Status "Setting environment variable ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP..."
try {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", $IPAddress, "User")
    Write-Success "Environment variable set: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
}
catch {
    Write-ErrorMsg "Failed to set environment variable: $_"
    exit 1
}

# Summary
Write-Status "Echo address discovery complete"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Configuration Summary:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Adapter:     $adapterName"
Write-Host "  IP Address:  $IPAddress"
Write-Host "  Echo IP Var: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Identify a network address for FactoryTalk Logix Echo communication and set ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP.

.DESCRIPTION
Rockwell QA64164 specifies that FactoryTalk Logix Echo controllers must use a Windows-configured
IPv4 address, not the loopback range (127.x.x.x). FactoryTalk Logix Echo can only bind a
controller to an IPv4 address Windows has already assigned to a NIC — it cannot invent a new
address on a subnet.

This script is READ-ONLY with respect to the network: it never adds, removes, or otherwise
modifies adapters or IP addresses, and never restarts services. It only inspects existing state
and helps you choose a value for ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP. Any NIC configuration (adding an address to
an adapter) or Windows service restart must be performed manually by an operator with
administrator privileges, per docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md.

This script:

1. Detects the adapter Echo is already using (an address currently assigned to a controller must
   never be reused) by matching a previously configured ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP, or lets you pick from
   the adapters currently present on this machine.
2. Queries Echo (via the harness's `echo-list-addresses` command) for every address a controller
   already holds.
3. Lists the IPv4 addresses already configured on the selected adapter and suggests one that no
   existing Echo controller is using — never proposing or accepting an address already claimed
   by a controller, and never a synthesized address that isn't actually configured on the NIC.
4. If every address already configured on the adapter is claimed by a controller, tells you a new
   address must be added to the NIC manually (this script will not do it) before Echo can use it.
5. Sets the environment variable ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP for test execution.

If Echo cannot bind an address (a "controller failed to set its IP address" or "not yet
synchronized" condition), the fix is to manually restart the FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message
Broker and Service (in that order: stop Service, stop Broker, start Broker, start Service) and
retry - see docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md. This script does not perform that restart.

.PARAMETER AdapterName
(Optional) The name of the adapter to inspect. If not specified, the script auto-detects the
adapter Echo is already using, or prompts you to choose from adapters present on this machine.

.PARAMETER IPAddress
(Optional) The static IPv4 address to use. If not specified, the script suggests an address
already configured on the chosen adapter that Echo is not currently using.

.EXAMPLE
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-echo-adapter.ps1
# Auto-detects the Echo adapter and suggests an existing address on it that Echo isn't using.

.EXAMPLE
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-echo-adapter.ps1 -AdapterName "Ethernet" -IPAddress "192.168.127.6"

.NOTES
Does not require administrator privileges. Performs no NIC or service changes.
#>

param(
    [string]$AdapterName,
    [string]$IPAddress
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Write-Status {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "`n[*] $Message" -ForegroundColor Cyan
}

function Write-Success {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[OK] $Message" -ForegroundColor Green
}

function Write-Warning {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[!] $Message" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

function Write-ErrorMsg {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[!!] $Message" -ForegroundColor Red
}

Write-Status "FactoryTalk Logix Echo Network Address Discovery"
Write-Host "Rockwell QA64164 requires a non-loopback IPv4 address for Echo communication."
Write-Host "This script does not modify any adapter or service; it only helps choose an address."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Guardrail: never reuse an IP address a controller already holds.
#
# Echo assigns controller addresses out of whichever adapter subnet is
# selected. If an operator has already configured a chassis/controller on an
# IP, colliding with it produces a hard-to-diagnose "address in use" or
# "not yet synchronized" failure much later in a test run. Detect existing
# Echo-assigned addresses up front and steer away from them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function Get-EchoAssignedAddresses {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns every IPv4 address FactoryTalk Logix Echo currently reports as assigned to a
    controller, via the test harness's "echo-list-addresses" command, or $null if it cannot be
    determined (harness not built, or Echo unreachable).
    #>
    $harnessExe = Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..\tests\harness") `
        -Recurse -Filter "LogixEchoHarness.exe" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $harnessExe) {
        return $null
    }

    try {
        $raw = & $harnessExe.FullName "echo-list-addresses" 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            return $null
        }
        if (-not $raw) {
            return @()
        }
        return @($raw | Where-Object { [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($_.Trim(), [ref]$null) })
    }
    catch {
        return $null
    }
}

function Select-UnusedAdapterAddress {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Return the first IPv4 address already configured on the adapter that Echo is not currently
    using for a controller.

    .DESCRIPTION
    FactoryTalk Logix Echo can only bind a controller to an IPv4 address that Windows has already
    assigned to a NIC (see IServiceApiClientV2.ListAvailableEthernetAddresses(), which enumerates
    configured addresses - it does not invent new ones on a subnet). The guardrail is therefore
    to pick among the adapter's EXISTING addresses, skipping whichever one(s) an existing Echo
    controller already holds, rather than synthesizing an arbitrary free host address that was
    never added to the NIC.
    #>
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$AdapterAddresses,
        [string[]]$InUse = @()
    )

    foreach ($candidate in $AdapterAddresses) {
        if ($candidate.StartsWith("127.") -or $candidate.StartsWith("169.254.")) {
            continue
        }
        if ($InUse -notcontains $candidate) {
            return $candidate
        }
    }

    return $null
}

# Get available adapters (read-only enumeration; nothing is created or changed)
$adapters = @(Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq "Up" -or $_.Status -eq "Disconnected" })

if ($adapters.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-ErrorMsg "No network adapters found on this machine."
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auto-detect the adapter Echo is already using, so a second/third controller
# lands on the same NIC instead of a caller picking an unrelated adapter.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$autoDetectedAdapter = $null
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName)) {
    Write-Status "Checking for an adapter Echo is already configured on..."
    $priorEchoIp = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", "User")
    foreach ($candidate in $adapters) {
        $existing = Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $candidate.Name -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("127.") -and -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("169.254.") }
        if ($existing -and $priorEchoIp -and ($existing.IPAddress -contains $priorEchoIp)) {
            $autoDetectedAdapter = $candidate.Name
            Write-Success "Found existing Echo adapter '$($candidate.Name)' (holds previously configured $priorEchoIp)"
            break
        }
    }
    if (-not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
        Write-Host "No previously configured Echo adapter found; you will be prompted to choose one."
    }
}

# If no adapter name provided, ask user to pick from adapters that already exist
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName) -and -not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Available network adapters:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $adapters | ForEach-Object -Begin { $i = 1 } -Process {
        Write-Host "  [$i] $($_.Name) - $($_.InterfaceDescription) (Status: $($_.Status))"
        $i++
    }
    Write-Host ""

    do {
        $choice = Read-Host "Select adapter [1-$($adapters.Count)]"

        if ([int]::TryParse($choice, [ref]$idx)) {
            if ($idx -ge 1 -and $idx -le $adapters.Count) {
                $selectedAdapter = $adapters[$idx - 1]
                $adapterName = $selectedAdapter.Name
                break
            }
        }

        Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid selection. Please try again."
    } while ($true)
} elseif ($autoDetectedAdapter) {
    $adapterName = $autoDetectedAdapter
} else {
    # Check if the requested adapter exists; this script never creates adapters
    $selected = $adapters | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $AdapterName }
    if ($selected) {
        Write-Success "Using adapter: $AdapterName"
    } else {
        Write-ErrorMsg "Adapter '$AdapterName' not found on this machine."
        Write-Host "This script does not create adapters. Available adapters:"
        $adapters | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $($_.Name) - $($_.InterfaceDescription)" }
        exit 1
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Determine which addresses on the target adapter are already in use by Echo,
# so the guardrail can suggest another address ALREADY CONFIGURED on the NIC
# that Echo is not using - not a synthesized free host address on the subnet.
# Echo can only bind a controller to an address Windows has already assigned
# to a NIC; it does not create new subnet addresses on its own, and neither
# does this script.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$existingAdapterIPs = @(
    Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $adapterName -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Select-Object -ExpandProperty IPAddress
)
$echoAssigned = Get-EchoAssignedAddresses
if ($null -eq $echoAssigned) {
    Write-Warning "Could not query Echo's currently assigned addresses (harness not built, or Echo unreachable)."
    Write-Warning "Falling back to only the adapter's configured addresses for collision avoidance."
    $echoAssigned = @()
}

if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Status "Adapter '$adapterName' has address(es) already configured:"
    $existingAdapterIPs | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $_" }
} else {
    Write-Warning "Adapter '$adapterName' has no IPv4 addresses configured."
    Write-Host "An administrator must add a non-loopback address to this adapter manually before"
    Write-Host "Echo can use it. This script will not do so."
}

# Choose an IP address if not provided
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($IPAddress)) {
    $suggested = Select-UnusedAdapterAddress -AdapterAddresses $existingAdapterIPs -InUse $echoAssigned

    if ($suggested) {
        Write-Host ""
        Write-Host "Address already configured on '$adapterName' that Echo is not using: $suggested" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        Write-Host "Press Enter to accept, or type a different non-loopback IPv4 address already on this NIC."
    } else {
        Write-Warning "Every address currently configured on '$adapterName' is already in use by an Echo controller."
        Write-Host "An administrator must manually add a new address to this NIC before Echo can use it"
        Write-Host "(this script will not modify the adapter). Once added, enter it below, or enter any"
        Write-Host "non-loopback IPv4 address already present on this adapter."
    }
    Write-Host "CRITICAL: Do NOT use loopback addresses (127.x.x.x) - they cannot be used with Logix Designer"
    Write-Host ""

    do {
        if ($suggested) {
            $entered = Read-Host "IP Address [$suggested]"
            if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($entered)) {
                $IPAddress = $suggested
            } else {
                $IPAddress = $entered
            }
        } else {
            $IPAddress = Read-Host "IP Address"
        }

        # Validate IP format
        if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
            Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format. Please try again."
            continue
        }

        # Reject loopback addresses (127.x.x.x)
        if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
            Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
            Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
            Write-Host ""
            continue
        }

        # Reject any address already claimed by an existing Echo controller.
        if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
            Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
            Write-Host "Choose a different address to avoid colliding with a PLC that is already configured."
            Write-Host ""
            continue
        }

        # Warn (but don't block) if the address isn't actually on the adapter yet - Echo
        # cannot use it until an administrator adds it manually.
        if ($existingAdapterIPs -notcontains $IPAddress) {
            Write-Warning "'$IPAddress' is not currently configured on adapter '$adapterName'."
            Write-Warning "An administrator must add it to the NIC manually before Echo can use it."
        }

        Write-Success "IP address: $IPAddress"
        break
    } while ($true)
} else {
    # Validate provided IP
    if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
        Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format: $IPAddress"
        exit 1
    }

    if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
        Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
        Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
        exit 1
    }

    if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
        Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
        Write-Host "Pick a different address; reusing an address in use by another PLC will break it."
        exit 1
    }

    if ($existingAdapterIPs -notcontains $IPAddress) {
        Write-Warning "'$IPAddress' is not currently configured on adapter '$adapterName'."
        Write-Warning "An administrator must add it to the NIC manually before Echo can use it."
    }

    Write-Success "Using IP address: $IPAddress"
}

# Set the environment variable for the test harness. This is the only change this script makes;
# it does not touch adapters, addresses, or services.
Write-Status "Setting environment variable ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP..."
try {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", $IPAddress, "User")
    Write-Success "Environment variable set: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
}
catch {
    Write-ErrorMsg "Failed to set environment variable: $_"
    exit 1
}

# Summary
Write-Status "Echo address discovery complete"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Configuration Summary:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Adapter:     $adapterName"
Write-Host "  IP Address:  $IPAddress"
Write-Host "  Echo IP Var: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Host "  Adapter addresses (unchanged): $($existingAdapterIPs -join ', ')"
}
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "To verify in PowerShell:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Get-NetAdapter -Name '$adapterName'"
Write-Host "  Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias '$adapterName' -AddressFamily IPv4"
Write-Host "  [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP', 'User')"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "If the chosen address is not yet on the adapter, an administrator must add it manually" -ForegroundColor Yellow
Write-Host "(this script performs no NIC changes)."
Write-Host "If Echo reports the controller could not set its IP address, an administrator should" -ForegroundColor Yellow
Write-Host "manually restart the FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message Broker and Service (stop Service,"
Write-Host "stop Broker, start Broker, start Service) and retry - see docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md."
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Note: Restart PowerShell to use the new environment variable in this session" -ForegroundColor Yellow

exit 0

+    if (-not $harnessExe) {
+        return $null
+    }
+
+    try {
+        $raw = & $harnessExe.FullName "echo-list-addresses" 2>$null
+        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
+            return $null
+        }
+        if (-not $raw) {
+            return @()
+        }
+        return @($raw | Where-Object { [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($_.Trim(), [ref]$null) })
+    }
+    catch {
+        return $null
+    }
+}
+
+function Select-UnusedAdapterAddress {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Return the first IPv4 address already configured on the adapter that Echo is not currently
+    using for a controller.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    FactoryTalk Logix Echo can only bind a controller to an IPv4 address that Windows has already
+    assigned to a NIC (see IServiceApiClientV2.ListAvailableEthernetAddresses(), which enumerates
+    configured addresses - it does not invent new ones on a subnet). The guardrail is therefore
+    to pick among the adapter's EXISTING addresses, skipping whichever one(s) an existing Echo
+    controller already holds, rather than synthesizing an arbitrary free host address that was
+    never added to the NIC.
+    #>
+    param(
+        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$AdapterAddresses,
+        [string[]]$InUse = @()
+    )
+
+    foreach ($candidate in $AdapterAddresses) {
+        if ($candidate.StartsWith("127.") -or $candidate.StartsWith("169.254.")) {
+            continue
+        }
+        if ($InUse -notcontains $candidate) {
+            return $candidate
+        }
+    }
+
+    return $null
+}
+
+# Get available adapters (read-only enumeration; nothing is created or changed)
+$adapters = @(Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq "Up" -or $_.Status -eq "Disconnected" })
+
+if ($adapters.Count -eq 0) {
+    Write-ErrorMsg "No network adapters found on this machine."
+    exit 1
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Auto-detect the adapter Echo is already using, so a second/third controller
+# lands on the same NIC instead of a caller picking an unrelated adapter.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+$autoDetectedAdapter = $null
+if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName)) {
+    Write-Status "Checking for an adapter Echo is already configured on..."
+    $priorEchoIp = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", "User")
+    foreach ($candidate in $adapters) {
+        $existing = Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $candidate.Name -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+            Where-Object { -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("127.") -and -not $_.IPAddress.StartsWith("169.254.") }
+        if ($existing -and $priorEchoIp -and ($existing.IPAddress -contains $priorEchoIp)) {
+            $autoDetectedAdapter = $candidate.Name
+            Write-Success "Found existing Echo adapter '$($candidate.Name)' (holds previously configured $priorEchoIp)"
+            break
+        }
+    }
+    if (-not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
+        Write-Host "No previously configured Echo adapter found; you will be prompted to choose one."
+    }
+}
+
+# If no adapter name provided, ask user to pick from adapters that already exist
+if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AdapterName) -and -not $autoDetectedAdapter) {
+    Write-Host ""
+    Write-Host "Available network adapters:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
+    $adapters | ForEach-Object -Begin { $i = 1 } -Process {
+        Write-Host "  [$i] $($_.Name) - $($_.InterfaceDescription) (Status: $($_.Status))"
+        $i++
+    }
+    Write-Host ""
+
+    do {
+        $choice = Read-Host "Select adapter [1-$($adapters.Count)]"
+
+        if ([int]::TryParse($choice, [ref]$idx)) {
+            if ($idx -ge 1 -and $idx -le $adapters.Count) {
+                $selectedAdapter = $adapters[$idx - 1]
+                $adapterName = $selectedAdapter.Name
+                break
+            }
+        }
+
+        Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid selection. Please try again."
+    } while ($true)
+} elseif ($autoDetectedAdapter) {
+    $adapterName = $autoDetectedAdapter
+} else {
+    # Check if the requested adapter exists; this script never creates adapters
+    $selected = $adapters | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq $AdapterName }
+    if ($selected) {
+        Write-Success "Using adapter: $AdapterName"
+    } else {
+        Write-ErrorMsg "Adapter '$AdapterName' not found on this machine."
+        Write-Host "This script does not create adapters. Available adapters:"
+        $adapters | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $($_.Name) - $($_.InterfaceDescription)" }
+        exit 1
+    }
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Determine which addresses on the target adapter are already in use by Echo,
+# so the guardrail can suggest another address ALREADY CONFIGURED on the NIC
+# that Echo is not using - not a synthesized free host address on the subnet.
+# Echo can only bind a controller to an address Windows has already assigned
+# to a NIC; it does not create new subnet addresses on its own, and neither
+# does this script.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+$existingAdapterIPs = @(
+    Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $adapterName -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+        Select-Object -ExpandProperty IPAddress
+)
+$echoAssigned = Get-EchoAssignedAddresses
+if ($null -eq $echoAssigned) {
+    Write-Warning "Could not query Echo's currently assigned addresses (harness not built, or Echo unreachable)."
+    Write-Warning "Falling back to only the adapter's configured addresses for collision avoidance."
+    $echoAssigned = @()
+}
+
+if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {
+    Write-Status "Adapter '$adapterName' has address(es) already configured:"
+    $existingAdapterIPs | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $_" }
+} else {
+    Write-Warning "Adapter '$adapterName' has no IPv4 addresses configured."
+    Write-Host "An administrator must add a non-loopback address to this adapter manually before"
+    Write-Host "Echo can use it. This script will not do so."
+}
+
+# Choose an IP address if not provided
+if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($IPAddress)) {
+    $suggested = Select-UnusedAdapterAddress -AdapterAddresses $existingAdapterIPs -InUse $echoAssigned
+
+    if ($suggested) {
+        Write-Host ""
+        Write-Host "Address already configured on '$adapterName' that Echo is not using: $suggested" -ForegroundColor Cyan
+        Write-Host "Press Enter to accept, or type a different non-loopback IPv4 address already on this NIC."
+    } else {
+        Write-Warning "Every address currently configured on '$adapterName' is already in use by an Echo controller."
+        Write-Host "An administrator must manually add a new address to this NIC before Echo can use it"
+        Write-Host "(this script will not modify the adapter). Once added, enter it below, or enter any"
+        Write-Host "non-loopback IPv4 address already present on this adapter."
+    }
+    Write-Host "CRITICAL: Do NOT use loopback addresses (127.x.x.x) - they cannot be used with Logix Designer"
+    Write-Host ""
+
+    do {
+        if ($suggested) {
+            $entered = Read-Host "IP Address [$suggested]"
+            if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($entered)) {
+                $IPAddress = $suggested
+            } else {
+                $IPAddress = $entered
+            }
+        } else {
+            $IPAddress = Read-Host "IP Address"
+        }
+
+        # Validate IP format
+        if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
+            Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format. Please try again."
+            continue
+        }
+
+        # Reject loopback addresses (127.x.x.x)
+        if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
+            Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
+            Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
+            Write-Host ""
+            continue
+        }
+
+        # Reject any address already claimed by an existing Echo controller.
+        if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
+            Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
+            Write-Host "Choose a different address to avoid colliding with a PLC that is already configured."
+            Write-Host ""
+            continue
+        }
+
+        # Warn (but don't block) if the address isn't actually on the adapter yet - Echo
+        # cannot use it until an administrator adds it manually.
+        if ($existingAdapterIPs -notcontains $IPAddress) {
+            Write-Warning "'$IPAddress' is not currently configured on adapter '$adapterName'."
+            Write-Warning "An administrator must add it to the NIC manually before Echo can use it."
+        }
+
+        Write-Success "IP address: $IPAddress"
+        break
+    } while ($true)
+} else {
+    # Validate provided IP
+    if (-not [System.Net.IPAddress]::TryParse($IPAddress, [ref]$null)) {
+        Write-ErrorMsg "Invalid IP address format: $IPAddress"
+        exit 1
+    }
+
+    if ($IPAddress.StartsWith("127.")) {
+        Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is a loopback address (127.x.x.x)."
+        Write-Host "Loopback addresses CANNOT be used with Logix Designer per Rockwell QA64164."
+        exit 1
+    }
+
+    if ($echoAssigned -contains $IPAddress) {
+        Write-ErrorMsg "REJECTED: '$IPAddress' is already assigned to an existing Echo controller."
+        Write-Host "Pick a different address; reusing an address in use by another PLC will break it."
+        exit 1
+    }
+
+    if ($existingAdapterIPs -notcontains $IPAddress) {
+        Write-Warning "'$IPAddress' is not currently configured on adapter '$adapterName'."
+        Write-Warning "An administrator must add it to the NIC manually before Echo can use it."
+    }
+
+    Write-Success "Using IP address: $IPAddress"
+}
+
+# Set the environment variable for the test harness. This is the only change this script makes;
+# it does not touch adapters, addresses, or services.
+Write-Status "Setting environment variable ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP..."
+try {
+    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", $IPAddress, "User")
+    Write-Success "Environment variable set: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
+}
+catch {
+    Write-ErrorMsg "Failed to set environment variable: $_"
+    exit 1
+}
+
+# Summary
+Write-Status "Echo address discovery complete"
+Write-Host ""
+Write-Host "Configuration Summary:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
+Write-Host "  Adapter:     $adapterName"
+Write-Host "  IP Address:  $IPAddress"
+Write-Host "  Echo IP Var: ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP = $IPAddress"
+if ($existingAdapterIPs.Count -gt 0) {
+    Write-Host "  Adapter addresses (unchanged): $($existingAdapterIPs -join ', ')"
+}
+Write-Host ""
+Write-Host "To verify in PowerShell:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
+Write-Host "  Get-NetAdapter -Name '$adapterName'"
+Write-Host "  Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias '$adapterName' -AddressFamily IPv4"
+Write-Host "  [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP', 'User')"
+Write-Host ""
+Write-Host "If the chosen address is not yet on the adapter, an administrator must add it manually" -ForegroundColor Yellow
+Write-Host "(this script performs no NIC changes)."
+Write-Host "If Echo reports the controller could not set its IP address, an administrator should" -ForegroundColor Yellow
+Write-Host "manually restart the FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message Broker and Service (stop Service,"
+Write-Host "stop Broker, start Broker, start Service) and retry - see docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md."
+Write-Host ""
+Write-Host "Note: Restart PowerShell to use the new environment variable in this session" -ForegroundColor Yellow
+
+exit 0

arguments.new_str:
The harness requires the `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` environment variable to be set to a non-loopback
address that is already configured on a Windows adapter (e.g. a static IP added to an existing
NIC, or a Microsoft Loopback Adapter such as `KM-TEST`). Adding that address to the adapter is a
manual, administrator-only step — see below.

**Guardrail: never collide with a PLC/controller Echo already has configured.** Echo can only
bind a controller to an IPv4 address that Windows has already assigned to a NIC — it does not
invent a free address on a subnet. If Echo is already running a chassis with a controller on a
given adapter/IP, that address is off-limits; reassigning it would break the existing controller.
`setup-echo-adapter.ps1` helps you pick a safe address, but **performs no network changes itself**
— it never adds/removes adapter addresses and never restarts services:

- Auto-detects the adapter already holding a previously configured `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP`, so a
  second controller lands on the **same NIC**.
- Queries Echo (via the harness's `echo-list-addresses` command) for every address a controller
  already holds.
- Lists the IPv4 addresses already configured on that adapter and suggests **one Echo is not
  using** — it never proposes or accepts an address already claimed by a controller.
- If every address already configured on the adapter is claimed, it tells you a new address must
  be added to the NIC manually; it will not add one itself.
- Sets the `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` environment variable to the chosen address.

Setup steps (required):

1. Run the read-only discovery script:
   ```powershell
   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File docs/runbooks/setup-echo-adapter.ps1
   ```

2. The script will:
   - Detect an adapter Echo is already using and default to it, or list adapters already present
     on the machine for you to choose from (it does not create adapters)
   - List the addresses already configured on that adapter and suggest one no existing Echo
     controller is using (e.g. if `.5`-`.9` are all configured and Echo is only using `.9`, it
     suggests `.5`), or accept a typed address
   - Warn if the chosen address is not yet configured on the adapter — an administrator must add
     it manually (`New-NetIPAddress`) before Echo can use it; the script will not do so
   - Set `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` environment variable

3. **Restart PowerShell** to activate the environment variable in your session.

4. Verify the setup:

The harness requires the `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` environment variable to be set to a non-loopback
address. The typical setup uses a Microsoft Loopback Adapter (KM-TEST) assigned a static IP like
`192.168.127.5`.

**Guardrail: never collide with a PLC/controller Echo already has configured.** Echo can only
bind a controller to an IPv4 address that Windows has already assigned to a NIC — it does not
invent a free address on a subnet. If Echo is already running a chassis with a controller on a
given adapter/IP, that address is off-limits; reassigning it (or removing it to make room) will
break the existing controller. Running `setup-echo-adapter.ps1` again:

- Auto-detects the adapter already holding a previously configured `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP`, so a
  second controller lands on the **same NIC**.
- Queries Echo (via the harness's `echo-list-addresses` command) for every address a controller
  already holds, then picks **another address already configured on that NIC** that Echo is not
  using — it never proposes or accepts an address already claimed by a controller.
- Only if every address already configured on the NIC is claimed does it fall back to adding a
  brand-new address to that adapter.
- **Never removes existing addresses** from the adapter. It only adds a new one when necessary,
  so a controller Echo already has running keeps working.

Setup steps (required):

1. Run the interactive adapter configuration:
   ```powershell
   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File docs/runbooks/setup-echo-adapter.ps1
   ```

2. The script will:
   - Detect an adapter Echo is already using and default to it, or list adapters / offer to
     create a new KM-TEST loopback adapter
   - Suggest an address already configured on that adapter that no existing Echo controller is
     using (e.g. if `.5`-`.9` are all configured and Echo is only using `.9`, it suggests `.5`),
     or accept a typed address
   - Only add a brand-new address to the NIC if every configured address is already claimed,
     **without removing** any address already assigned
   - Set `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` environment variable

3. **Restart PowerShell** to activate the environment variable in your session.

4. Verify the setup:
   ```powershell
   [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP', 'User')
   ```

automatically once if the first attempt to add the address fails; force it up front with:

67. It still holds controllers. Delete every controller first, then the chassis.
68. 
69. **Connection timeout on the comm path**
70. Two usual causes: the `EmulateEthernet\` prefix is missing, or the IP address was read before
71. `CreateController` returned. The address is only valid after the controller exists.
72. 
73. **Controller log says `Failed to set IP address`**
74. Confirm the address is configured on the Echo host and is returned by
75. `IServiceApiClientV2.ListAvailableEthernetAddresses()`. Rockwell QA64164 supports a static
76. address on a Microsoft KM-TEST adapter; select it with `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` rather than excluding
77. virtual adapters. Restart Echo after a network change — `setup-echo-adapter.ps1` does this
78. automatically if the first attempt to add the address fails, or force it up front with
79. `-RestartEchoServices`. If the controller's `Root/output.log` still reports `Failed to set IP
80. address` for both that address and an active physical-adapter address, preserve the logs and
81. escalate as an Echo installation/runtime fault. Do not edit Echo's `model.xml`.

1. # Troubleshooting
2. 
3. Symptoms first. Each entry names the layer that produced it.
4. 
5. ## Rockwell VCS explode / implode
6. 
7. **`VCS source implode failed`**
8. Do not build or commit the tree. Run `acd.ps1 -FromDir ... -ToL5X ... -Force` directly and
9. inspect the preceding `l5xgit` diagnostic. Confirm the source has
10. `RSLogix5000Content/RSLogix5000Content.xml` and `export-options.yaml`.
11. 
12. **`Refusing to write into non-empty directory`**
13. `l5xgit explode` guard. Confirm the target path, then pass `-Force` to `acd.ps1`. Check the path
14. first because the existing source directory will be replaced.
15. 
16. **`Tag data is in L5K format`**
17. The L5X was exported with undecorated data. Re-export from Studio 5000 with decorated tag data.
18. 
19. **`TargetType is not Controller`**
20. A partial export. The pipeline requires a full-application export.
21. 
22. **Explode creates a broad metadata-only diff**
23. Confirm the pinned VCS revision, Studio revision, and `export-options.yaml`. Keep serializer
24. upgrades separate from controller logic changes.
25. 
26. ## ACD conversion
27. 
28. **`l5xgit was not found`**
29. Build the pinned Rockwell VCS tools revision from
30. [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) and set `ACS_L5XGIT_PATH` to the resulting
31. `l5xgit.exe`, or add its directory to `PATH`.
32. 
33. **`acd.ps1` fails with a licence error**
34. Studio 5000 is not activated on the runner, or the activation server is unreachable.
35. 
36. **Conversion hangs**
37. Studio 5000 is showing a modal dialog on a session nobody can see. Run the runner service as a
38. named account rather than LocalSystem. Kill `LogixDesigner.exe` to clear it.
39. 
40. **`Controller type not supported`**
41. The project targets something other than a ControlLogix 5580. See
42. [../testing/logix-echo-setup.md](../testing/logix-echo-setup.md).
43. 
44. ## Logix Echo
45. 
46. **`Controller assigned loopback address (127.x.x.x) — communication fails`**
47. This is Rockwell QA64164: Echo can assign loopback addresses by default, but Logix Designer
48. cannot communicate with them. Configure a Microsoft KM-TEST loopback adapter with a static IP
49. address (e.g., `192.168.127.10`) and set `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` to use it.
50. 
51. ```powershell
52. # From repo root (requires admin)
53. powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File docs/runbooks/setup-echo-adapter.ps1
54. 
55. # Verify
56. Get-NetAdapter -Name "KM-TEST"
57. [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", "User")
58. ```
59. 
60. Then restart PowerShell for the environment variable to take effect.
61. 
62. **`Chassis not found` immediately after `CreateChassis`**

arguments.new_str:
**`Controller assigned loopback address (127.x.x.x) — communication fails`**
This is Rockwell QA64164: Echo can assign loopback addresses by default, but Logix Designer
cannot communicate with them. An administrator must manually configure a non-loopback IPv4
address on a Windows adapter (e.g. a static IP on a Microsoft KM-TEST loopback adapter, such as
`192.168.127.10`), then set `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` to it.

```powershell
# Discover/choose an address (read-only; no admin required, makes no network changes)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File docs/runbooks/setup-echo-adapter.ps1

# If the chosen address is not yet on the adapter, an administrator adds it manually, e.g.:
#   New-NetLoopbackAdapter -Name "KM-TEST"                      # one-time, admin required
#   New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "KM-TEST" -IPAddress "192.168.127.10" -PrefixLength 24

# Verify
Get-NetAdapter -Name "KM-TEST"
[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP", "User")
```

Then restart PowerShell for the environment variable to take effect.

data.content:
Removed all admin-required NIC/service mutation logic from the agent-run script and re-verified it works end-to-end unelevated.

Changes:
- **[setup-echo-adapter.ps1](/C:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-CI-CD/docs/runbooks/setup-echo-adapter.ps1)** rewritten to be strictly read-only against the network: removed the admin check, `New-NetLoopbackAdapter`, `New-NetIPAddress`, `Enable-NetAdapter`, and `Restart-EchoServices`/`-RestartEchoServices` entirely. It now only enumerates existing adapters (`Get-NetAdapter`) and their existing IPs (`Get-NetIPAddress`), queries Echo's assigned addresses via the harness, suggests/validates an address, warns if manual admin action is needed (adding an address to the NIC, or restarting Echo services), and sets `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` — its only actual side effect.
- Updated [logix-echo-setup.md](/C:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-CI-CD/docs/testing/logix-echo-setup.md), [troubleshooting.md](/C:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-CI-CD/docs/runbooks/troubleshooting.md), and [test-harness.instructions.md](/C:/Users/MitchellLandreth/Git-Local/AB-Logix-CI-CD/.github/instructions/test-harness.instructions.md) to describe the script as read-only/advisory, with NIC changes and Echo service restarts framed as manual, admin-only operator steps.
- Validated syntax and ran the script live (unelevated) against the real `Ethernet` adapter — it correctly listed the 5 existing addresses, suggested one, and set the env var with zero network/service mutation.
